goal: Adds a persistent per-key label (by master key fingerprint) so multisig participants and hardware wallets can be identified, with new RPCs and GUI interfaces to set, get and list labels.
reviewability: Not ready right now: the author marked the PR draft and said it will stay open until the project decides whether key labels should exist at all.
agreement: Unresolved objection from achow101 (maintainer): scope mismatch with what was discussed and a correctness objection that fingerprints are collidable, not addressed with a fix (achow101).
Additional skepticism about value versus maintenance cost (rkrux).
Concept and approach support from several reviewers who tested the RPCs (jeanpablojp, Eunovo, vicjuma).
Author agrees the concept needs to be settled first and paused the PR pending that decision (polespinasa).

result.summary: This PR adds a new wallet database record mapping a master key fingerprint to a label, three new RPCs (setkeylabel, getkeylabel, listkeylabels), extensions to getaddressinfo and gethdkeys to surface those labels, and four new interfaces::Wallet methods so a future GUI can consume the same functionality, e.g. to name multisig participants or hardware wallets. It includes a new functional test covering single-key and multisig scenarios, plus release notes.
result.problem: Users setting up multisig wallets or using multiple hardware devices currently have no built-in way to remember which key belongs to which participant or device; this PR proposes storing that association in the wallet itself so both RPC and future GUI consumers can show it consistently.

open_concerns: achow101 (maintainer): the design does not match what was discussed for key labeling (GUI-only, ephemeral during multisig setup, not persisted) and separately objects that fingerprints are collidable and unsuitable as the storage key; neither point has been addressed with a code change.
rkrux: skeptical that RPC-level key labeling is a priority compared to a guided multisig GUI flow, and questions whether the maintenance burden is justified.
Eunovo: setkeylabel silently overwrites an existing label without warning (author says this mirrors setlabel behavior and considers it a UX, not RPC, concern).

jeanpablojp: raised multiple correctness gaps in multi-key descriptor handling (sortedmulti, taproot script paths) that were fixed during review, and questioned whether interfaces::Wallet methods with no caller should exist.
resolved_concerns: Multisig getaddressinfo failing to report key labels for sortedmulti/taproot script-path descriptors was fixed by adding a per-key key_labels object.
Ambiguous fingerprint-to-label resolution order (non-deterministic winner) was fixed per author confirmation ('good catch, fixed').
Typos in release notes flagged by maflcko were fixed.
Test assertion gaps flagged by jeanpablojp were incorporated by the author.
discussion.author_status: Author (polespinasa) marked the PR as draft on 2026-09-10, stating it will stay open while the project decides whether key labels should be included at all, and that the PR is 'not in a rush to get merged'.

uncertainties: Whether the project ultimately decides to persist key labels at all is unresolved; if the concept is rejected, this PR's priority in wallet would drop toward zero regardless of code quality.
Whether achow101's fingerprint-collision objection is fatal to the current design or fixable by switching the storage key (e.g., to full pubkey) is not yet discussed in the thread.
result.card: This PR adds a persistent per-key label keyed by master key fingerprint to the wallet database, three new RPCs (setkeylabel/getkeylabel/listkeylabels), extensions to getaddressinfo and gethdkeys, and four new interfaces::Wallet methods for a future GUI to show friendly names for multisig participants or hardware wallets. The problem it targets is real but narrow: helping users identify which key belongs to which cosigner or device, a feature the author notes exists in wallets like Sparrow. A maintainer (achow101) issued a concept NACK, objecting both that persistent storage was not what was discussed (the GUI-only, ephemeral design) and that using collidable fingerprints as the storage key is unsound; another reviewer (rkrux) questions the value versus maintenance cost. Several other reviewers gave Concept/Approach ACKs and tested the RPCs. The author has paused the PR as draft pending a project decision on whether key labels should exist at all, so it is not currently reviewable for merge-readiness though the underlying design question is worth resolving.
